reference_opening.argument: This video is non-scam content because it instructs viewers how to use Instagram settings and the Report a Problem feature to submit an account issue or feedback. The visible actions involve selecting a support category, typing feedback, and sending it, while the requests to subscribe and visit TechBoomers.com are ordinary audience engagement and website promotion, not conditions for receiving Instagram support.

citations.quote: If you want to contact Instagram customer support, we'll show you how.
Start by opening the Instagram app on your device.
On the next screen, scroll down and tap Report a Problem
From the menu that appears, select the nature of your issue
On the next screen type in the details of your issue or question. When you're done, hit send.

opening.argument: The video pairs a low-barrier benefit with an explicit click-through request. Its description advertises “over 100 free courses,” while the closing screen tells viewers to click to go to TechBoomers.com. That creates a simple acquisition pathway: take the viewer action, reach the promoted site, and obtain the advertised free course material. The same description also directs viewers to an online contact form and social-media pages, reinforcing that the instructional framing is being used to drive viewers toward external destinations rather than merely explain Instagram settings.

citations.quote: over 100 free courses on all of today's most popular websites & apps!
You can fill out Instagram's online contact form here: https://help.instagram.com/contact/364531043625021

rebuttal.rebuttal: The defense describes the Instagram navigation accurately, but that does not answer the solicitation embedded around it. The video ends with a direct invitation to click through to TechBoomers.com, and the description promotes free courses and multiple external contact destinations. Those calls to action are not necessary to demonstrate the Report a Problem feature; they give the tutorial a separate acquisition purpose.

citations.quote: Visit http://www.techboomers.com for over 100 free courses on all of today's most popular websites & apps!

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The quoted material shows promotion, but it does not show that clicking, subscribing, or visiting the site is required to receive a reward, payment, withdrawal, or asset. “Free courses” describes educational material, and the Instagram instructions are completed inside the app through “Report a Problem.” The external links therefore do not establish a scam promise-action relationship.

citations.quote: To contact Instagram, go to your Settings, then scroll down and tap Report a Problem.
And that's all there is to contacting Instagram customer service.

opening.argument: Several risk signals appear together: the description supplies an email address, an online contact-form URL, and social-media destinations, while also acknowledging that people who email “do not receive a response.” It then promotes a separate website with more than 100 free courses. That combination of external destinations, a low-friction free offer, and a warning that the advertised email route may not respond makes the viewer dependent on links and promotional claims rather than a clearly accountable support channel. The closing screen compounds the concern by asking viewers to subscribe and click through to the promoted site.

citations.quote: However, most people who try to contact Instagram through email do not receive a response.
You can email them at [EMAIL].
You can fill out Instagram's online contact form here: https://help.instagram.com/contact/364531043625021

rebuttal.rebuttal: The defense focuses on ordinary taps in Instagram, but it leaves the risk signals unexplained. The description admits that the email route generally produces no response, then presents several other external routes and a separate free-course promotion. A viewer is consequently steered among links and calls to action whose reliability the video does not establish, rather than receiving a self-contained support resolution.

citations.quote: most people who try to contact Instagram through email do not receive a response.
Here are some other ways to get in touch with Instagram:

true_side_reply.rebuttal: These are not concealed risk signals: the description plainly identifies the destinations and explicitly warns that email often receives no response. The online form and social pages are presented as alternative ways to contact Instagram, while the course promotion is separate. Nothing quoted promises money, an asset, or an unusually easy financial return for clicking or subscribing.

citations.quote: Here are some other ways to get in touch with Instagram:
Reach out to Instagram on their social media pages:

opening.argument: Although presented as customer-support education, the video also operates as a promotional funnel for TechBoomers. The speaker identifies herself as being from TechBoomers.com, invites viewers to take further courses, asks for a thumbs-up, and directs them to the site. The description repeats that promotion with a text version and a promise of over 100 free courses, while the final frame displays both a subscription button and a click-through to TechBoomers.com. The Instagram demonstration therefore supplies useful subject matter and credibility for a broader solicitation to engage with the publisher.

citations.quote: I'm Jessica from TechBoomers.com.
If you'd like to learn more about Instagram and how to use it, check out our free Instagram course on techboomrs.com.
Thanks for watching. If you found this video helpful, we'd love it if you'd click the thumbs up button below.

rebuttal.rebuttal: Calling the ending ordinary engagement understates how prominently the promotion is integrated. The speaker identifies with TechBoomers, sends viewers to a free Instagram course, requests a thumbs-up, and the closing screen places subscription and site-click prompts alongside the branded tutorial. The support lesson can therefore be read as promotional content designed to convert attention into visits and subscriptions.

citations.quote: check out our free Instagram course on techboomrs.com.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The promotional elements are openly attributed to TechBoomers and do not promise money, withdrawal, or an asset in exchange for participation. The speaker's request for a thumbs-up and invitation to an educational course are ordinary audience engagement. Most importantly, the substantive demonstration remains an Instagram support workflow, ending when the issue is submitted.

citations.quote: On the next screen type in the details of your issue or question. When you're done, hit send.
And that's all there is to contacting Instagram customer service.
